1.steps:
1) Configure a VPN policy on the local firewall using IKE Main mode.Select LAN Primary subnet object from a drop-down menu under Local Networks.Select Remote Net from a drop-down menu under Destination Networks (the address object is created previously, it is a LAN of the remote firewall).Check the Apply NAT Po licies checkbox in the Advanced tab.reate a new address object Loc Translated (same class as LAN) and select it in the Translated Local Network drop-down menu.Select Original in the Translated Remote Network drop-down menu.
 2) Configure a VPN policy on the remote firewall using IKE Main mode.elect LAN Primary subnet object from a drop-down menu under Local Networks.Create a new address object Rem Translated (same network that was defined for local translated network on the local firewall, zone VPN) and select it from a drop-down menu under Destination Networks.
 3) Send pings to translated local network from a remote host.
1.title: one firewall translates local network
1.result: When the VPN policy on the local firewall applies NAT policies, a new policy is created on the Network > NAT Policies page of the local firewall. It has LAN Primary Subnet as a source original, Loc Translated as a source translated, Remote Net as a destination original, and Original as a destination translated. The address objects in LAN to VPN and VPN to LAN access rules are Loc Translated and Remote Net. When the remote host sends pings to the local translated address, the SA in IKE Main mode is negotiated. The local firewall shows the active tunnel on the VPN > Settings page with the translated subnet under Local and remote LAN under Remote. The pings are returned. The remote firewall shows the active tunnel on the VPN > Settings page with its LAN under Local and remote translated network under Remote. The appropriate log messages are generated on the both firewalls. The log shows the translated network is proposed by the local firewall.

4.steps:
1) Add a custom zone, name it NewZone. Assign an interface to the NewZone.
 2) Create a group object. Add the NewZone interface and LAN. Nam e the group Loc LAN and NewZone.
 3) Create address objects, Translated LAN specifies zone LAN and network of the same class as LAN. Translated NewZone specifies zone NewZone and network of the same class as the subnet on the NewZone. Combine those two address objects into a new group object. Nam e the group object Loc Translated LAN and NewZone.
 4) Configure a VPN policy on the local firewall using IKE Main mode. Select ?Loc LAN and NewZone? object from a drop-down menu under Local Networks. Select Remote Net from a drop-down menu under Destination Networks (the address object is created previously, it is a LAN of the remote firewall, zone - VPN). Check the Apply NAT Policies checkbox in the Advanced tab. Select Loc Translated LAN and NewZone in the Translated Local Network drop-down menu. Select Original in the Translated Remote Network drop-down menu.
 5) Configure a VPN policy on the remote firewall using IKE Main mode. Select LAN Primary subnet object from a drop-down menu under Local Networks. Create a new group object Rem Translated LAN and NewZone (group address objects, same networks that were defined for local translated networks on the local firewall, zone VPN) and select it from a drop-down menu under Destination Networks.
 6) Send pings to two translated local networks from a remote host.
4.title: One firewall translates local networks defined as a group object
4.result: When the VPN policy on the local firewall applies NAT policies, new policy is created on the Network > NAT Policies page of the local firewall. The policy has Loc LAN and NewZone as a source original, Loc Translated LAN and NewZone as a source translated, Remote Net as a destination original, and Original as a destination translated. The address objects in LAN to VPN and VPN to LAN access rules on the local box are ?Loc Translated LAN and NewZone and Remote Net. When the remote host sends pings to the local addresses on two translated networks, the SA in IKE Main mode is negotiated. The local firewall shows the active tunnel on the VPN > Settings page with the translated local subnets under Local and remote LAN subnet under Remote. The pings are returned. The remote firewall shows the active tunnel on the VPN > Settings page with its local LAN subnet under Local and translated remote subnets under Remote. The appropriate log messages are generated on the both firewalls. The log shows the translated networks are proposed by the local firewall.
